concepts.title: Biodiversity and Its Loss
concepts.definition: We share the planet with millions of living beings from micro-organisms and lichens to banyan trees, elephants and blue whales; this biodiversity is threatened as species vanish fastest today - through habitat destruction, hunting, poaching, over-exploitation, environmental pollution and forest fires.
concepts.key_idea: Species vanish faster now than ever before - and the causes are human.
concepts.textbook_ref: jess102.txt opening sections on biodiversity and its loss
question_patterns: what is biodiversity - why does it matter for human survival
list the causes of depletion of forest and wildlife resources
how does habitat destruction endanger species - explain

why are tigers and other large mammals hunted - discuss poaching
explain how environmental pollution threatens biodiversity

solution_steps.explain: Biodiversity ranges from microbes to whales across every habitat.
Habitat loss, poaching, pollution and fires drive species to extinction.
Forest-dwelling communities often bear the cost of conservation.

concepts.title: Conservation of Forests and Wildlife
concepts.definition: Conservation safeguards the dwindling variety: the Indian Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 created schedules of protected species, national parks and sanctuaries, and projects like Project Tiger - while newer approaches involve local communities in Joint Forest Management so that protection and livelihoods go together.
concepts.key_idea: Protect by law, involve by livelihood: acts, parks and Joint Forest Management together.
concepts.textbook_ref: jess102.txt sections on conservation of forests and wildlife
question_patterns: what is the Indian Wildlife Protection Act - state its provisions
describe Project Tiger and its purpose
what is Joint Forest Management - how do communities participate
how do national parks and sanctuaries protect wildlife
give an example of successful community conservation from the chapter

solution_steps.explain: Acts and schedules place species and habitats under protection.
Parks and sanctuaries reserve entire ecosystems.
Joint Forest Management shares protection duties and benefits with villagers.

concepts.title: Types and Distribution of Forests
concepts.definition: Forests are classified by management into reserved forests, protected forests and unclassed forests; India's forest cover is judged against the target of one-third of land area, and distribution varies sharply across states and regions.
concepts.key_idea: Reserved, protected, unclassed: management status decides how safely a forest lives.
concepts.textbook_ref: jess102.txt sections on types and distribution of forests
question_patterns: differentiate reserved, protected and unclassed forests
what proportion of land should be under forest according to the national policy

why are reserved forests important for conservation
compare the forest cover of the given states
how does classification of forests help in their management

solution_steps.explain: Reserved forests get the strongest protection, unclassed the least.
The national goal is one-third forest area; many regions fall short.
Forest wealth concentrates unevenly across states and districts.
